opportunities.title: Authors' Contingency Fund
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Professional authors resident in the UK or British citizens (fiction writers, illustrators, literary translators, scriptwriters, poets, journalists and others) for whom author-related activities make up a substantial amount of their annual income. Not open to editors, copywriters, or those with salaried income for writing. Membership of the SoA not required. Repeat applicants must wait four full calendar years since last grant.
opportunities.summary: Hardship grants to authors in financial difficulty, providing small short-term grants in moments of crisis to help them return to normal working practice. Can be used for lost income, shortfalls from failed projects, impact of illness, changes to homelife, or one-off expenses such as a boiler or laptop. Assessed on a rolling basis (decision within two weeks).

opportunities.title: Authors' Foundation
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Writers who have been previously published or have a contract for their project with a commercial UK or Irish publisher. For book projects: commissioned by a commercial UK/Irish publisher, or have had at least one book commercially published of which they are sole author/translator. For script projects: previously professionally performed on stage/screen/radio in UK/Ireland or under contract. Non-contributory contracts required. Hybrid/self-published books not eligible. Recipients must wait four years before re-applying.
opportunities.summary: Grants to help develop a work-in-progress. Accepts fiction, non-fiction, poetry and script projects. No deadlines; submissions accepted on a rolling basis. Applicants are also automatically considered for specific named awards (Eric Ambler, Taner Baybars, John Brooks, Antonia Fraser, Arthur Welton, Great Britain Sasakawa Grant).

opportunities.title: K Blundell Trust
opportunities.eligibility_summary: British authors under 40 (under 40 on Sunday 1 March 2026), British by birth and currently resident in the United Kingdom. Must have a previous work of which they are the sole author published with a commercial UK publisher. Recipients must wait four years before re-applying. Cannot apply for both K Blundell Trust and Authors' Foundation in the same calendar year.
opportunities.summary: Work-in-progress grants for British authors under 40 whose work aims to increase social awareness. Accepts fiction, non-fiction, poetry and script projects. Currently closed and will re-open for applications in 2027.

opportunities.title: Society of Authors' Access Fund

amount.raw: small grants (usually £150 or less); applications over £150 accepted but may take longer

opportunities.eligibility_summary: All authors (anyone who creates work for publication, broadcast or performance). Open to UK and Irish residents and British and Irish citizens. Membership not required but applicants should meet SoA membership criteria. One grant per calendar year.
opportunities.summary: Small grants for travel, subsistence, childcare or carer support, and other access needs for events, residencies and retreats. Assessed on a rolling basis. Currently closed for applications and expected to re-open in 2027.

opportunities.title: Strachey Trust Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: All authors (as defined by SoA Full Membership criteria, membership not required) who are UK resident or British citizens, working on a specific full-length literary project with a strong likelihood of publication. One application per calendar year; successful applicants must wait four years before re-applying.
opportunities.summary: Grants to enable authors to travel to a UK or Republic of Ireland archive or collection to research manuscript material for a specific full-length literary project with a strong likelihood of publication. Assessed on a rolling basis (usually within two weeks).
